course_description: Learning a second language not only involves understanding the structure of that language, but also learning how language is used for different purposes across a range of different contexts and modalities. In this course, you will study language from the point of view of its users, the choices they make and constraints they encounter in using language in different settings, and the effects of their use of language on other people. You will also study how what is meant always goes well beyond what is simply said or written. Drawing from research in discourse and pragmatics, this course will give you an overview of the way language is used in different communicative situations, and illustrate how meaning that goes beyond what is said is constructed relative to contexts. You will analyse a number of key pragmatic dimensions of language use, including reference, information structure and presupposition, inference and implicature, and speech acts, and examine how the pragmatics of second languages are learned. While the data used in the course will come primarily from English, the theoretical perspectives and analytical methods employed have implications for the acquisition and teaching of all second languages.

course_aims: In SLAT7810, we will explore how language can be used to convey various layers of meaning, with a particular focus on language use in second language contexts. The course explores the different types of meaning and actions that can be delivered through language, and the implications of this for the learning and teaching of second languages.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify different features of pragmatic meaning
Understand the systematic ways in which language can be used to deliver actions
Effectively apply the concepts and theories studied in this course to the analysis of language use across different contexts
Critically reflect on the implications of the concepts and theories studied in this course for the learning and teaching of second languages

assessment_details.task_description: Each week, from WEEK 2 to 7 and 9 to 12, students will need to complete an online Weekly Quiz consisting of 3 questions. These quizzes will be available every Wednesday on Blackboard and must be submitted by 5pm on Friday of the same week. The questions will cover the lecture material and required readings for that week. Each Weekly Quiz will contribute 3% to the final grade. After completing all ten quizzes, the total score will be calculated. Answers to the questions will be marked as correct or incorrect. For each correct answer, students will receive 1 point. assessment_details.task_description: This assessment item involves two parts. Part I: Video Presentation (20 marks). You will record a 10-minute presentation in which you critically analyse one pragmatic phenomenon examined in this course. You should: Clearly define and contextualise the chosen concept (e.g., implicature, reference, speech acts, etc.) Engage with relevant theories and key readings from the course Provide and analyse authentic or constructed examples Critically evaluate how meaning is shaped in context (e.g., social, cultural, interactional factors) You must upload this video by Monday 5:00pm in Week 13. Part II: Tutorial Interview (20 marks). In Week 13, you will attend your tutorial and participate in a short individual interview with your tutor about your presentation. During this interview, you will be asked questions designed to: Check your understanding of the key concepts and arguments in your presentation Clarify and extend your analysis Reflect on relevant theoretical perspectives and readings This is a closed-book and no-device 5-minute interview.
